comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4 and C49 regarding clinical response data. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the RECIST response analysis supported, with OpenEval noting statistical significance and peer reviewers acknowledging the association with clinical outcomes without specific critique.

Strong disagreement on claims C87-C89 regarding DUX4 expression thresholds. OpenEval finds the methodological decisions supported and reasonable, while peer reviewers (R1 and R3) find them UNSUPPORTED, criticizing inconsistent thresholds across analyses, exclusion of 126 intermediate patients, and lack of prospective rationale.

Partial disagreement on survival analysis claims C5-C6, C51-C60, C74. OpenEval finds the multivariate Cox regression and model validation rigorous and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the analyses are 'fairly convincing' but raising critical concerns about the exclusion of intermediate DUX4 patients (n=126) and inconsistent categorization thresholds impacting rigor.

Strong agreement on claims C61-C68, C70-C72 regarding RSF analysis. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the random survival forest methodology, feature importance metrics, and Shapley value analysis well-conducted and SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers noting it is 'quite interesting and well conducted.'

Disagreement on transcriptomic immune findings C34-C44. OpenEval finds comprehensive SUPPORTED evidence across multiple pathways and analyses. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for overlapping claims C35-C39, C41-C44, acknowledging findings are 'clear and unambiguous' but critically noting 'this is an association and does not demonstrate causality,' questioning the mechanistic interpretation.

Disagreement on IHC validation claims C3, C45-C46. OpenEval finds the immunohistochemistry data SUPPORTED as direct validation of transcriptomic findings. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for broader set including these claims, accepting the data quality but emphasizing the observational nature precludes causal conclusions.

Disagreement on DUX4 expression in metastatic vs primary tumors (C2, C25-C26). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with converging evidence from multiple cohorts. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the finding is 'striking' but questioning the comparison validity since TCGA melanoma contains mostly locoregional metastatic samples (367 vs 81 primary), requesting further stratification analysis.

Perfect agreement on methodological validation claims C29-C31. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the matched FFPE/frozen sample analysis SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers explicitly stating it is 'a nice validation' showing differences are not due to preservation or sequencing artifacts.

Agreement on uncertainty for clinical utility claims C84-C85. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting pan-cancer applicability is inferred and IHC screening utility is speculative. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether DUX4 provides additional information beyond other immune markers and critiquing the binary categorization approach.

Agreement on RNA-seq coverage analysis claims C27-C28. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as confirming full-length transcript expression. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this technical finding (SUPPORTED) without raising concerns, supporting the functional interpretation.

Agreement on mechanistic interpretation claim C78. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on RNA-seq coverage and citations to prior STAT1 inhibition studies. Peer reviewers accept this technical finding (SUPPORTED) regarding full-length vs truncated transcripts without critique.

OpenEval finds claim C50 regarding TMB and survival SUPPORTED as a positive control validating the cohort. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this claim, though it relates to the broader survival analysis context.

OpenEval finds claims C79-C81 regarding time-dependent Shapley values SUPPORTED, showing temporal variation in feature importance with ECOG PS dominating early and DUX4 becoming more important later. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these temporal dynamics claims.

OpenEval finds claims C1, C7-C24, C33, C40, C47-C48, C75-C76, C86 providing background context SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background and contextual claims.
